Description: Continue - The server has received the request headers and the client should proceed to send the request body.
Switching Protocols - The requester has asked the server to switch protocols and the server has agreed to do so.
Processing - The server has received and is processing the request but no response is available yet.
Early Hints - The server is providing preliminary response headers while it prepares the final response.
OK - The request succeeded.
Created - The request succeeded and a new resource was created as a result.
Accepted - The request has been received but not yet acted upon.
Non-Authoritative Information - The returned metadata is not exactly the same as is available from the origin server.
No Content - There is no content to send for this request but the headers may be useful.
Reset Content - The request succeeded and the client should reset the document view or input form.
Partial Content - This response code is used when the Range header is sent from the client to request only part of a resource.
Multi-Status - The response contains status information for multiple resources or operations. Inspect the WebDAV response body for individual results.
Already Reported - Members of a WebDAV binding have already been included earlier in the multi-status response.
Multiple Choices - The request has more than one possible response.
Moved Permanently - The URL of the requested resource has been changed permanently. Check the Location header for the new URL.
Found - The URI of the requested resource has been changed temporarily. Check the Location header.
See Other - Retrieve the requested resource from the URI in the Location header using a GET request.
Not Modified - The resource has not been modified since the version specified by the request headers.
Temporary Redirect - The server sends this response to direct the client to get the requested resource at another URI.
Permanent Redirect - The resource is now permanently located at another URI specified by the Location header.
Bad Request - The server cannot process the request due to client error (e.g. malformed syntax). Verify request format and parameters.
Unauthorized - Authentication is required and has failed or has not been provided. Check credentials and authentication tokens.
Forbidden - The client does not have access rights to the content. Verify permissions and authorization settings.
Not Found - The server cannot find the requested resource. Verify the URL and ensure the resource exists.
Method Not Allowed - The request method is not supported for the requested resource. Check allowed HTTP methods for this endpoint.
Not Acceptable - The requested resource is not available in a format that respects the Accept headers. Adjust Accept headers.
Proxy Authentication Required - Authentication with the proxy is required. Check proxy credentials and the Proxy-Authenticate header.
Request Timeout - The server timed out waiting for the request. Retry the request or check network connectivity.
Conflict - The request conflicts with the current state of the server. Review and resolve the conflicting state.
Gone - The requested resource is no longer available and will not be available again. Remove references to this resource.
Length Required - The server requires a valid Content-Length header. Supply the request body length and retry.
Precondition Failed - One or more conditions specified in the request headers evaluated to false. Verify conditional headers such as If-Match and If-Unmodified-Since.
Payload Too Large - The request entity is larger than limits defined by server. Reduce request payload size.
URI Too Long - The URI requested by the client is longer than the server is willing to interpret. Shorten the URI.
Unsupported Media Type - The media format of the requested data is not supported. Check Content-Type header.
Range Not Satisfiable - The requested byte range cannot be fulfilled. Verify the Range header against the resource size.
Expectation Failed - The server cannot meet the requirements of the Expect request header. Remove or revise the expectation.
I'm a Teapot - The server refuses to brew coffee because it identifies as a teapot.
Misdirected Request - The request was sent to a server that cannot produce a response for the target authority. Retry using a different connection.
Unprocessable Content - The request syntax is valid but its instructions cannot be processed. Correct validation or semantic errors in the request body.
Locked - The requested WebDAV resource is locked. Release the lock or supply the correct lock token.
Failed Dependency - The request failed because a dependent WebDAV operation failed. Resolve the earlier failure and retry.
Too Early - The server is unwilling to process a request that might be replayed. Retry after the secure connection is fully established.
Upgrade Required - The server requires a different protocol. Follow the Upgrade header and retry with the required protocol.
Precondition Required - The server requires the request to be conditional. Supply an appropriate header such as If-Match.
Too Many Requests - Rate limit exceeded. Implement backoff and retry after the time specified in Retry-After header (or exponential backoff if no header indication).
Request Header Fields Too Large - The request headers are too large. Reduce header size or remove unnecessary cookies and retry.
Unavailable For Legal Reasons - Access to the resource is denied for legal reasons. Review the response for details about the restriction.
Internal Server Error - The server encountered an unexpected condition. Contact support or check server logs for details.
Not Implemented - The request method is not supported by the server. Use a different HTTP method.
Bad Gateway - The server received an invalid response from the upstream server. Check upstream server status and connectivity.
Service Unavailable - The server is not ready to handle the request (maintenance or overload). Retry after some time or check service status.
Gateway Timeout - The server acting as a gateway did not get a response in time. Retry or increase timeout settings.
HTTP Version Not Supported - The server does not support the HTTP version used by the request. Use a supported protocol version.
Insufficient Storage - The server cannot store the representation needed to complete the request. Free storage or reduce the operation size.
Loop Detected - The server detected an infinite loop while processing a WebDAV request. Correct the resource bindings or request path.
Network Authentication Required - The client must authenticate to gain network access. Complete the captive portal or network sign-in.
